feature: CCNA Switching: VLAN and access ports
scenarioChecks: Practice starts with four administratively down VLAN 1 interfaces and no task credit
Published interface-range commands create named VLANs and assign both access-port groups
Both same-VLAN pairs exchange real simulated ICMP traffic in both directions
ARP broadcast flooding reaches only the correct same-VLAN port and never the other VLAN pair
Cross-VLAN pings fail with no inter-VLAN routing or host default gateway
Wrong VLAN assignment or shutdown breaks the affected pair while the other VLAN pair remains operational; repair restores it
The MAC task requires all four received dynamic entries in their expected VLANs and ports
Clear/relearn and saved reloads require fresh MAC learning while earned ping tasks persist
Every published IOS and Windows verification command returns the documented success or expected cross-VLAN loss
Portable copies, renamed nodes and device power cycles retain working VLAN and host configuration
